rules.when: (?=[\s\S]*\[(?P<limits>\d+)\] Card dispute time limits)(?=[\s\S]*\[(?P<credit>\d+)\] Provisional credit)[\s\S]*Is a debit card dispute for goods not received within the time limit after 9 days, and is provisional credit due\?
rules.text:
Yes on both counts.

- **Time limit:** a debit card transaction can be disputed up to 90 days after it posts [{limits}], so 9 days is well inside it.
- **Provisional credit:** give it within 10 business days of a complete dispute of 25.00 CAD or more on a personal card [{credit}]. For goods not received, a complete dispute names the expected delivery date [{credit}].
- **Approval:** at 482.10 CAD it is under the 1,000.00 CAD analyst limit, so no team lead is needed unless the account was opened in the last 30 days [{credit}].

Next step: get the expected delivery date from Jordan, then start the Card dispute intake workflow.

rules.when: (?=[\s\S]*\[(?P<notice>\d+)\] Restraining notices and levies)(?=[\s\S]*\[(?P<exempt>\d+)\] Funds exempt from a levy)[\s\S]*How much does a restraining notice hold, and which funds are exempt from a levy\?
rules.text:
Hold funds in every deposit account the debtor owns, up to twice the amount the notice names, from the moment the notice arrives [{notice}]. For a 3,250.00 CAD notice that is up to 6,500.00 CAD.

Never hold [{exempt}]:

- government benefit deposits from the last 60 days (pension, disability, child benefit, employment insurance)
- the first 2,500.00 CAD in a personal account

Work out the exempt amount first and hold only what is above it, then send the customer the exemption notice within 2 business days [{exempt}]. Answer the creditor within 5 business days with the accounts found and the amount held [{notice}].
